thread.title: Dow Rises, Nasdaq Falls as Tea Leaves Point to a Choppy Year-End

title: Dow Rises, Nasdaq Falls as Tea Leaves Point to a Choppy Year-End
text:
Dow Rises, Nasdaq Falls as Tea Leaves Point to a Choppy Year-End By Nov. 5, 2018 12:39 p.m. ET Order Reprints Illustration by Michael Haddad Text size
Wait and See . Stocks were mixed to start the week, as tech suffered fresh losses and all eyes shifted to Tuesday’s midterm elections. In today’s Intraday Update we... ...check in on earnings; ...theorize about whether the year will end with a bang or a whimper. ...and see what’s boosting Starbucks (SBUX).
Indecision 2018
Stocks were moving in opposite directions Monday, with the Dow Jones Industrial Average up 0.5%, the S&P 500 climbing 0.2%, and the Nasdaq Composite lagging behind with a 1.2% decline.
It may be November, but October’s shadow looms long: While all three indexes were able to end last week with gains , worries remain. Apple ’s (ticker: AAPL) lackluster outlook continues to weigh on tech. Newsletter Sign-up
Still, plenty of optimism remains, as the Dow and S&P work their way higher. Glenmede’s Jason Pride writes that his firm sees just a 16% change of recession in the next year, leading him to believe that the market’s October slide was “yet another correction amidst an ongoing expansion.”
Certainly, that has been the opinion of investors watching yet another banner earnings season unfold. Although reports were light to start the week, we’re still in the thick of third-quarter results. “U.S. companies are once again delivering stronger results than their global peers,” writes Credit Suisse ’s Jonathan Golub, with S&P 500 companies increasing earnings by 16.3% (excluding tax benefits).
Of course, as we’ve learned, investors are after more than just the numbers this time around. While second-quarter results were enough to buoy stocks, the focus on commentary has become more intense, given a host of growing worries from trade to global growth. Tariffs, wage inflation, and rising interest rates are three major threats to the S&P 500’s “all-time high” profit margins, writes Goldman Sachs ’ David Kostin, although on conference calls this quarter, management teams have been confident about offsetting costs via price increases or supply-chain reorganization. “However, executives noted increased competition for labor and intensifying wage pressures,” he said “Transcripts also revealed managers were preparing for further tightening of financial conditions by strengthening their balance sheets. We recommend investors favor firms with strong pricing power.”
Macro worries aside, however, double-digit earnings growth is still encouraging. But that’s a double-edged sword, warns The Leuthold Group’s Jim Paulsen. He argues that “fabulous profit results” and “fantastic fundamentals” have been a major underpinning of stocks’ rise in recent years despite numerous risks, but consensus expectations for a 10% rise in earnings next year might be too rosy, given weak global growth and higher costs for capital and labor. “Saying farewell to a trusted friend and guardian (solid profitability) is never easy, and...the stock market may yet have further to fall,” says Paulsen.
Not surprisingly, Morgan Stanley ’s Michael Wilson, who has been cautious for some time, agrees. He says that the third quarter could mark the peak for earnings. Therefore, while “most of the price damage is done, for now”, liquidity is “unlikely to improve, making it a potentially choppy ride for the rest of 2018,” he writes.
Of course, plenty of others have more upbeat hopes for the remainder of the year. Yet with the midterms Tuesday, a U.S.-China meeting scheduled later this month, and another expected interest-rate increase next month, choppiness doesn’t seem like a tall order.
Midday Movers
Barrick Gold (ABX) is down 0.5% to $13.11 and Newmont Mining (NEM) is down 1.2% to $32.05 on reports the companies may combine their Nevada gold assets .
Fiat Chrysler Automobiles (FCAU) rose 1.1% to $16.36 after Societe Générale upgraded it to Buy.
International Business Machines (IBM) gained 3.8% to $120.10 after several insiders disclosed stock purchase, including a nearly $1 million buy by CEO Virginia Rometty.
Starbucks (SBUX) climbed 1% to $64.93. Mizuho upgraded it to Buy.
Under Armour (UAA) rallied 1.8% to $24.13 after Piper Jaffray upgraded it to Outperform.
